title: Synthetic Golden Streams + Canary Rollback Orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build an orchestrator that ties canary and A/B rollouts to live evaluation against curated golden prompt streams (synthetic and real traffic), automatically triggering rollback or mitigation when composite scorecards cross configurable regression thresholds. This aims to reduce latent quality regressions escaping canaries while keeping noise low for small-volume customers.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: design and implement the orchestration layer, metrics computation pipeline for golden streams, sampling/weighting logic for shadow traffic, console UI for thresholds and alerts, and automated rollback hooks into the deployment controller. Also include audit logs and per-customer golden assignments.
- Non-goal: end-to-end model training validation or large-scale offline eval tooling (those remain in Research).

Key concepts:
- Synthetic Golden Streams: a maintained set of golden prompts representative of high-RPM workloads and edge cases. Streams include both static golden sets and recent high-value customer prompts (anonymized/consented).
- Composite Scorecard: multi-metric signal combining semantic similarity (embedding drift), generation-quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable), hallucination heuristics, and business KPIs (API error rate, latency anomalies). Each metric is normalized and weighted; weights are configurable per-project.
- Canary Orchestrator: orchestrates incremental traffic shifts, attaches shadow copies to the candidate model, computes scorecards in near-real-time, and evaluates gating rules to decide pass/fail/hold/rollback.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Real-time vs batch scoring: we opted for streaming near-real-time scoring for golden prompts (sub-minute windows) to catch regressions quickly. This increases compute cost; we mitigate via sampling and prioritized golden sets.
- Synthetic vs real prompts: synthetic golden prompts cover deterministic edge cases; sampled anonymized customer prompts increase coverage of real-world behavior. We will store customer-derived prompts for a rolling 90-day window and allow opt-out.
- Thresholds and sensitivity: default composite threshold is conservative (higher tolerance) for canaries <=5% traffic and stricter for >5%. Teams can override by release.
- Rollback policy: multi-step (auto-mitigation -> freeze -> rollback). Immediate automatic rollback only when composite score decline exceeds hard-fail threshold and secondary signals (latency/ERR) also spike. Otherwise, orchestrator marks canary as "Hold" and paginates on-call with context.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data pipelines: golden stream ingestion, anonymization, and routing to scoring workers. (ENG-22134 dependency for routing infra)
2) Scoring workers: lightweight feature extraction (embeddings, token-level heuristics) and score aggregation. Use quantized embedding models for cost.
3) Orchestrator service: exposes REST hooks for rollout controller, stores per-rollout score history, evaluates gating rules, triggers rollback via deployment API.
4) Console UI: new "Canary guards" panel in Console with real-time scorecards, timelines, and manual override controls.
5) Audit & Compliance: per-customer logs, KMS references for any stored prompts, and a review workflow for customer-sourced golden sets.

APIs and config knobs:
- rollout.attach_golden_set(rollout_id, golden_id, sampling_rate)
- rollout.set_scorecard_thresholds(rollout_id, {composite:0.85, hard_fail:0.70})
- rollout.enable_shadow(rollout_id, percent)
- orchestration.get_rollout_history(rollout_id)

Acceptance criteria:
- Scoring pipeline ingests synthetic golden set and produces composite scores within 45s of generation for >=90% of events.
- Orchestrator evaluates gated canary rollout and triggers auto-rollback when composite score decline >15% and secondary signal count >3 in 2 windows.
- Console shows historical scorecards, a per-golden breakdown, and a one-click rollback action for owners.
- Audit logs for every automated decision with links to underlying prompts and scoring snapshots.

Operational metrics to monitor:
- Time-to-detect (median/95th) for regressions on golden streams.
- False positive rollback rate (target < 1% of rollouts).
- Cost per 100k scored prompts (budget targets to be defined by FinOps).

Security and privacy:
- Customer-derived prompts are hashed and stored only when customer consents; plaintext is stored only in a KMS-wrapped S3 bucket with ACLs.
- Role-based access controls for viewing golden prompt contents in Console.

Rollout plan and milestones:
- Week 1-2: proto scoring worker + synthetic golden ingestion (internal-only).
- Week 3-4: orchestrator MVP with canary attach hook and basic auto-fail.
- Week 5: Console integration + opt-in for a small pilot (2 internal teams).
- Week 6-7: production hardening, security review, broader beta with selected customers.

Longer-term ideas (out of scope for initial iteration): auto-generated augmentation of golden sets, per-customer baseline personalization, and ML-driven threshold tuning.
